data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump 'surprised' UK freed air base suspects on bail
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Trump 'surprised' UK freed air base suspects on bail
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that British police should not have released on bail five men who were arrested near an air base used by the United States over a suspected attack.
Trump added that the case "might be" linked to Iran but declined to give details.
"I'm surprised that they released them; I wouldn't have done that," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, while adding that British authorities had worked "very closely" with the US.
"We know everything about them. We would not have released them."
The five men were arrested early on Sunday near the Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford base in southwest England, from which US bombers have taken off to target Iran since March.

data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israeli settlers attack Palestinian homes, assault residents in Halhul, north of Hebron
Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian homes and assaulted several residents under the protection of Israeli forces on Monday night, local time, in the town of Halhul, north of Hebron, Wafa reported.
The report said that a group of armed settlers, protected by Israeli forces, attacked homes and assaulted several residents in the Wadi Qaboun area of the town.
Israeli forces also set up a military checkpoint at the town’s entrance, searched passing vehicles, and checked passengers’ identification cards.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel security agency files complaint over report Netanyahu visited UAE
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israel security agency files complaint over report Netanyahu visited UAE
Israel's domestic security service filed a complaint against a TV channel that reported Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the UAE, his office said Monday, the government's first acknowledgement of the trip despite not naming the destination.
"This evening the Shin Bet filed a complaint with the Chief Military Censor, demanding that Channel 12 be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law following a severe censorship violation," read a statement from Netanyahu's office, which oversees the security agency.
On Sunday, Channel 12 and other Israeli media outlets reported that Netanyahu had visited the Gulf country to meet with President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
Neither country has confirmed Netanyahu visited the UAE, with Monday's statement the first acknowledgement of any kind by Israel.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Netanyahu asked UAE leader to publicly deny 7 October 2023 warning to Israel: Report
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Netanyahu asked UAE leader to publicly deny 7 October 2023 warning to Israel: Report
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu travelled to the UAE on Sunday to ask Emirati President Mohamed bin Zayed to publicly deny a story that the Gulf state warned him in advance of the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, according to a report by the Associated Press.
Netanyahu lobbied the UAE president in an “hour-long” meeting to deny reporting by Haaretz that said he was warned Hamas was planning a major operation, according to Israeli media outlets.
The report, published by Haaretz based on an upcoming book, said Zayed had told Netanyahu that Israel should be ready for a Hamas-led attack. The Emirati leader also recommended trying to find an economic solution to the besieged Gaza Strip and calm tensions in the occupied West Bank, where Israeli settlers have attacked Palestinians with impunity and dramatically expanded illegal settlements.

The release of the five - all London-based Britons in their mid-20s - came as Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an emergency meeting of top officials to ensure they have "the full picture".
Earlier, Iran had denied involvement in any plot to target the Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford base, following the security scare there early Sunday.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli army set off large explosion in south, report says
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Israeli army set off large explosion in south, report says
The Israeli military set off a significant explosion in the southern Lebanese village of Mansouri on Monday, Lebanese state media and AFP reported.
"A massive explosion rocked the town of Mansouri in the Tyre district a short while ago. The explosion was carried out by Israeli occupation forces," Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported.
"The sound of the explosions was heard in the city of Tyre and several surrounding villages," the NNA added.
AFP correspondents saw large clouds of smoke emerge from the largely destroyed town after the loud explosion was heard.
The town of Mansouri, located around nine kilometres (six miles) south of Tyre and 10 kilometres north of Israel, and its surroundings were subjected to several Israeli strikes and to artillery shelling in recent weeks despite a ceasefire that took hold in June.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran supreme leader says US will be forced out of Middle East
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Iran supreme leader says US will be forced out of Middle East
Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Monday that the United States would be forced to leave the Middle East after suffering "painful blows", according to a statement carried by state television.
Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the start of the war in late February, made the remarks despite attempts to revive talks aimed at ending the fighting.
"Today, having suffered painful blows at the hands of valiant fighters and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they (the enemies) do not venture beyond the Arabian Sea," Khamenei said in the written statement attributed to him, without explicitly mentioning the United States.
"Whenever they have braved this risk, they have only brought harm upon themselves. It will not be long before the Arabian Sea, too, would rid itself of their presence," he added.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Palestinian-American journalist freed after 13 days in Israeli detention
data.author: Qazi Zaid
data.summary:
Palestinian-American journalist freed after 13 days in Israeli detention
Palestinian-American journalist Naqaa Hamed was released from Damon Prison after 13 days, following an Israeli court decision.
Hamed was arrested on 15 September at the Tuqu checkpoint while returning from an assignment. She was separated from her camera crew and taken to an unknown location for questioning.
According to Israeli media, Hamed was arrested on suspicion of “cooperating with an enemy entity” and possible espionage. She had previously served as a correspondent for Iran’s Press TV in the occupied West Bank.
According to the Palestinian Prisoners’ Society, 36 Palestinian journalists, including four women, remain detained in Israeli jails, along with about 90 Palestinian women.

Araghchi to meet mediators in talks with US amid efforts to reopen Hormuz
Iran’s ISNA news agency reported that Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and a delegation will meet with mediators involved in talks with the United States on Monday morning.
The latest proposals and views on the situation will be discussed during the talks, ISNA said.
A Qatari delegation has been in the United States and presented Washington with an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for economic relief.
Iran's Tasnim news agency said there were no plans for direct talks between Iranian and US officials.
The meetings come as Washington and Tehran continue to trade proposals over the strategic waterway amid increased tensions.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel shuts Palestinian shops to facilitate Jewish prayers in Jerusalem’s Old City
data.author: Qazi Zaid
data.summary:
Israel shuts Palestinian shops to facilitate Jewish prayers in Jerusalem’s Old City
Israeli forces have ordered dozens of Palestinian shops in the Old City of occupied East Jerusalem to close, restricting access to streets leading to the Al-Aqsa Mosque.
The closure covers more than 50 shops and took effect on Sunday morning, the third day of the Sukkot holiday. It is due to remain in place until 2 October.
The shops are located in the Muslim Quarter, along streets leading to Bab al-Qattanin (Cotton Merchants' Gate), one of the main gates to Al-Aqsa used by Palestinian worshippers.
On Sunday night, hundreds of Israelis gathered in the area for holiday rituals.
Palestinian residents were ordered to remain indoors, while the Bab al-Qattanin leading to Al-Aqsa was closed.

data.author: Bilge Kotan

Labour conference blocks motion to cancel Palantir contract over Israeli army links
The Labour Party’s Conference Arrangements Committee (CAC) has blocked an emergency motion brought by party delegates on cancelling Palantir’s NHS contract over the company’s links to the Israeli military.
The motion, put forward at the party’s conference in Liverpool by the Labour-affiliated Socialist Health Association and at least three constituency parties, urged the government to cancel the £330m ($437m) contract to process NHS data with the controversial tech giant.
It said Palantir was “facing numerous allegations of involvement in serious breaches of human rights, including due to it developing technology for Israel's military to use in its unlawful occupation of Palestinian land and genocide in Gaza".

data.author: Qazi Zaid

US Centcom rejects IRGC claim of ‘complete control’ over Hormuz
Iran does not fully control the Strait of Hormuz, US Central Command said, hitting back against claims from a senior Iranian military commander that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps “completely controls” the strategic waterway
In a post on X, Centcom said claims that “Iran has full control over the Strait of Hormuz … are false”. It added: “Iran has no navy because American forces sank it.”
According to Centcom, more than 1 billion barrels of oil have recently passed through the strait, demonstrating that Iran does not control the waterway.
American forces have been helping to keep commercial traffic flowing through the strait while enforcing a blockade on Iranian maritime trade, US officials have said previously.

data.author: Qazi Zaid
data.summary:
Netanyahu asks UAE president to deny warning before 7 October attack
During a meeting in Abu Dhabi on Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu asked UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan to refute a report that he had warned Israel of an impending Hamas attack before the 7 October attack in 2023, The Associated Press reported.
The meeting came after a report in the Israeli newspaper Haaretz that the Emirati leader had warned Netanyahu of a planned Hamas operation days before the Hamas-led attack.
The UAE foreign ministry declined to comment on the latest report, saying it maintains “open and direct lines of communication” with Israel and shares “all relevant intelligence”.
The AP report said there was no immediate comment from Netanyahu’s office on the meeting or his request to bin Zayed.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli football chiefs weigh sacking coach after 'humiliating' 3-0 loss to Ireland
data.author: Nadav Rapaport
data.summary:
Israeli football chiefs weigh sacking coach after 'humiliating' 3-0 loss to Ireland
Submitted by
Nadav Rapaport
on
Mon, 09/28/2026 - 13:21
Israeli commentators called the first-half collapse in Hungary one of the most shameful nights in the national team's history, after the visiting side had weighed a boycott over the genocide in Gaza
Republic of Ireland's James Abankwah in action with Israel's Manor Solomon , Israel v Republic of Ireland - Nagyerdei Stadion, Debrecen, Hungary - 27 September 2026 (Reuters/Bernadett Szabo)
Off
Israel's 3-0 defeat to the Republic of Ireland on Sunday has prompted a wave of recrimination in Israeli football. Commentators called it one of the most shameful nights in the national team's history, and the Israel Football Association (IFA) is weighing whether to dismiss its head coach.
Sources in the IFA told Israeli news site Ynet that they expected Ran Ben-Shimon to resign as the result "wasn't just another sporting defeat, it was a humiliation for every Israeli and Jew".
The match was played in Debrecen, Hungary. Ireland's players had weighed a boycott over the genocide in Gaza and decided only on Saturday, the day before kick-off, to take part. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew, citing "the atrocities in the region".
The teams did not shake hands before the match. Ireland's players bowed their heads during Israel's national anthem and wore black armbands in recognition of "all lives lost in the conflict", Irish broadcaster RTE reported.
Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan all scored in the first half. Israel was the home side, but the match was played in front of largely empty stands.
"In tough times, that's where you find your leaders, that's where characters step up," Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE after the game. "I think everybody that has watched the game saw proud Irishmen fight for their nation."
